edition.title: This weekend on Keowee + Jocassee
edition.dek: Jazz on the Alley names its act this time: Nathan Angelo plays Ram Cat Alley Thursday. From there the weekend gets crowded in a good way — Hannah Harper plays two nights at Walhalla PAC, Westminster throws its annual Bigfoot Festival, and Oconee County runs its Veterans Appreciation Festival Saturday. Both breweries keep their usual Friday–Saturday music going underneath all of it, and Jocassee Valley Brewing closes things out Sunday afternoon.

events.title: Jazz on the Alley: Nathan Angelo
events.body: The city's October lineup is out, and this week's headliner is Nathan Angelo. Same free-and-easy setup as always — the Happy Hour Showcase warms up the street, then the main act takes over.
events.note: Free · Happy Hour Showcase 5:30–6:30pm, Nathan Angelo 7–9pm · Ram Cat Alley, downtown Seneca

events.title: SC Bigfoot Festival
events.body: Westminster's main street turns over to Bigfoot for the weekend — live music, vendors, Sasquatch-themed competitions, speakers, and kid stuff, running Friday into Saturday. It's a drive from the lake, but it's the kind of unabashedly weird regional event worth the trip once.
events.note: Free to attend · Fri–Sat, times TBD — check the operator · Main Street, Westminster

events.title: Hannah Harper, two nights at Walhalla PAC
events.body: The rising country act plays back-to-back shows Friday and Saturday — same set time both nights. Walhalla PAC's room is small enough that it never feels like a big-venue show, which is most of its appeal.
events.note: $59–$79 · 7:30pm both nights · Walhalla Performing Arts Center, 101 E. North Broad St, Walhalla

events.title: Veterans Appreciation Festival & Ride of Honor
events.body: Oconee County's 5th annual Veterans Festival adds a first this year: the Ride of Honor, a motorcycle ride held the same day. Start time and route weren't posted when we checked — the festival's Facebook page is the best source before you head out.
events.note: Check the operator for times · Oconee County

events.title: Brewery music carries on underneath it all
events.body: If Bigfoot and the Veterans Festival aren't your Saturday, both breweries run their usual live-music night: Jocassee Valley Brewing has Alma Russ with the Pachuys food truck, and Keowee Brewing has its regular Friday–Saturday set (check their calendar for who's playing — it wasn't posted by name when we checked).
events.note: Free · Jocassee Valley Brewing music 6:30pm · Keowee Brewing music 6:30–8:30pm

events.title: Jocassee Valley Brewing closes the weekend
events.body: Marshall Goers and Lucy Allen play an early-evening set with Majoes Filipino food out front — a calm landing after a loud Saturday.
events.note: Free · Music at 4pm · open 12–7pm · Jocassee Valley Brewing, Salem

plan.title: Eat first, then pick your Friday
plan.body: Grab dinner before deciding: Hannah Harper's first night at Walhalla PAC, or the drive out to Westminster for Bigfoot Festival's opening night.
plan.label: Find a spot to eat & drink →

plan.title: Launch early — Saturday's the busy one
plan.body: Between Bigfoot Festival, the Veterans Festival, and both breweries' music nights, Saturday has more pulling at it than usual. Get on the water in the morning before any of it starts.
plan.label: Find a ramp →

plan.title: A swim, then let Jocassee Valley close it out
plan.body: Nothing else dated during the day — pick a swim spot, check today's lake level, and save Marshall Goers and Lucy Allen's set for late afternoon.
